gallery.filename: Aufruf zum Dankgottesdienst der Deutschen Christen.jpg
gallery.title: File:Aufruf zum Dankgottesdienst der Deutschen Christen.jpg
gallery.description:
A propaganda publication by the pro-Nazi Protestant movement Deutsche Christen ('German Christians'), printed shortly after Adolf Hitler was appointed Chancellor on January 30, 1933. It presents Hitler’s rise as a divinely granted victory, urging believers to thank God for the political outcome. The text mixes Christian language with Nazi ideology, portraying Hitler as the leader chosen by God and calling for a special thanksgiving church service. A telegram from the movement’s leader, Pastor Hossenfelder, congratulates Hitler and promises the movement’s loyalty and prayers. Overall, the document reflects how the “German Christians” tried to religiously legitimize the Nazi regime and integrate Christian worship into Nazi political celebration.
Evangelium in the Third Reich for Greater Berlin
Volume 2, No. 6 — Sunday, 5 February 1933
“With us the victory, with us the battle cry: Germany Awake! Germany, you are free!”
These words from the Sturmlied of Wilhelm Rube have so often echoed heavenward as a sacred oath during the years of humiliation and disgrace. Yes, we believed in victory, we fought for victory, and our Lord God granted us victory. Today our Führer Adolf Hitler stands at the head of the German Reich as Reich Chancellor.
After all the struggle and all the bloody sacrifices of the past fourteen years, our hands fold for a moment, and quietly our hearts—filled with gratitude—recall Martin Rinckart’s simple prayer of thanks:
“Now thank we all our God with hearts and hands and voices, Who wondrous things has done, in whom this world rejoices.”
Whoever thinks in this way and wishes to thank God with us is invited to attend the thanksgiving service announced below at St. Mary’s Church (Marienkirche).
— Karl Fahrenhorst
“The Faith Movement German Christians”
The Faith Movement “German Christians” is holding a thanksgiving service on Friday, 3 February 1933, at St. Mary’s Church, at 8 p.m.
The sermon will be given by the national leader (Reichsleiter), Pastor Joachim Hossenfelder.
All National Socialists and German Christians who wish to thank God with us for the “victory” of 30 January 1933—that is, the seizure of power—are to take part in this service.
Telegram from our National Leader to the Führer of the new Germany, Adolf Hitler
I congratulate you and the German people on the outcome of 30 January, shaped—so it is said—by God’s providence. As national leader of the Faith Movement “German Christians,” I assure you that our prayers stand behind you.
— Hossenfelder
